reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that compound stimuli do not uniformly contribute to habit strength; rather, their individual contributions are modulated by stimulus type and temporal dynamics. This leads to a vectorial model of habit formation where each stimulus aggregate contributes a scalar ΔH. The weighting matrix W encapsulates these differential contributions, enabling a linear algebraic representation of cumulative habit loadings. Dynamic elements generate higher ΔH due to ongoing neural adaptation, whereas static elements saturate quickly. These primitives form a dual framework: one for probabilistic inference (GSI) and another for sequential decision-making (GSE). The failure mode occurs when static elements dominate, causing stagnation in habit evolution. The mathematical structure supports both Bayesian updating and Markovian policy transitions.
